summary.text: The council layers record flood plain and coastal inundation intersections, with coastal inundation covering 0.5% of the parcel, while tsunami evacuation zones and coastal erosion mapping also intersect it.

The council maps shallow landslide classes of High and Very Low, large-scale classes of Low and Very Low, and liquefaction vulnerability of Very Low here; its landslide ratings do not measure risk for an individual property.
Your standard loan scenario falls within high loan-to-value ratio (LVR) and high debt-to-income ratio (DTI) lending, for which the Reserve Bank limits the share of new bank lending.
The rules assessment marks the First Home Loan scenario as eligible, subject to lender assessment; the Reserve Bank exempts First Home Loans from its LVR and DTI restrictions.
The title type remains unresolved because multiple title types were returned, and the council valuation and build era could not be checked because there was no unique council property match.

next_steps.text: Check the council property file for geotechnical reports, or ask a geotechnical engineer for site-specific advice.
Ask your lender how it applies the low-deposit lending limit and what extra costs apply.
Ask your lender how it calculates your debt-to-income ratio.
Ask your lender which lending criteria it applies to First Home Loan applications.
Ask the council or your insurer what the coastal inundation mapping means for this property.
Ask your lawyer to obtain and review the LIM report and other property documents from the council.
